title: Morning light
science_note: Morning light sets your body clock and raises cortisol at the right time.

tiny.text: Step outside and face the sky. No sunglasses.

standard.text: Go outside in your first hour awake: 5–10 min on a clear day. Look toward the sky, not at the sun. No sunglasses.

stretch.text: Stay 10 min. Partly cloudy: 15 min. Overcast: 30 min.

todo: Tiny '1 min' comes from the Figma Busy day sheet, not from the book.

title: Same sleep times
science_note: A steady sleep and wake time improves sleep quality.

tiny.text: Set tomorrow's wake alarm to your usual time.

standard.text: Go to bed and wake up at the same time, within 30 min.

stretch.text: Keep the same times on weekends too.

todo: SL04b (1-week chronotype test) is a task, not included here.

title: Caffeine cutoff
science_note: Caffeine blocks the sleep signal (adenosine) and stays in your body for hours.

tiny.text: Pick a decaf drink for your afternoon cup.

standard.text: No caffeine in the 10 hours before bed. Best: none after 14:00.

stretch.text: No caffeine in the 12 hours before bed. Stay under 400 mg a day.

todo: Needs are [sleep] only, from the symptom map in engine-spec section 1. Table 2-A lists 'sleep energy' for SL11 as a whole.
Default cutoff bed−10h is an open decision in engine-spec (#1).

title: Delay coffee
science_note: Waiting a bit for coffee can help prevent the afternoon energy crash.

tiny.text: Drink a glass of water first. Coffee can wait.

standard.text: Have your first coffee 60 min after waking.

stretch.text: Have your first coffee 90 min after waking.

todo: Needs are [fog, energy], from the symptom map in engine-spec section 1 (SL11b is listed under Foggy and Always tired).
Skip this patch on mornings with a hard workout right after waking (book note).

title: Daily steps
science_note: Daily walking is the base for heart and brain health.

tiny.text: Stand up and walk to the nearest window.

standard.text: Reach 7,000 steps today.

stretch.text: Reach 10,000 steps today.

title: Walk after meals
science_note: A short walk after eating keeps blood sugar lower and cuts the sleepy dip.

tiny.text: Stand up and take a few steps after you eat.

standard.text: Walk 5–10 min within 30 min after a meal.

stretch.text: Walk 10–30 min after a meal.

title: Air squats
science_note: Squats wake up your leg muscles and get blood moving again.

tiny.text: Stand up from your chair once, slowly.

standard.text: 10 air squats (no weights).

stretch.text: 10 air squats every 45 min of sitting.

title: Sitting break
science_note: Long sitting switches off muscles and slows your metabolism.

tiny.text: Soleus pushups: while seated, lift and lower your heels.

standard.text: Move for 5 min after 30 min of sitting.

stretch.text: Move 5 min for every 30 min of sitting, all work day.

todo: Exact Soleus pushup description should be copied from the book file (engine-spec open item).

title: Water on waking
science_note: Your body is low on water after sleep.

tiny.text: Drink one glass of water.

standard.text: Drink 500 ml of water after waking, before coffee or breakfast.

stretch.text: Drink 700 ml of water after waking, before coffee or breakfast.

title: Daily water
science_note: Low water lowers focus.

tiny.text: Fill a water bottle and put it on your desk.

standard.text: Drink 2.4 L of water in your first 10 hours awake.

stretch.text: 2.4 L in 10 hours, spread out: a glass every hour.

title: Protein at meals
science_note: Protein keeps you full and protects muscle.

tiny.text: Add one protein food, like a yogurt.

standard.text: Eat 30–50 g of protein at this meal.

stretch.text: 30–50 g of protein at every full meal today.

todo: duration_min = 5 comes from Figma (Pick patches: 'Protein breakfast · 5 min'), not engine-spec.

title: Physiological sigh
science_note: A double inhale and a long exhale slows your heart rate fast.

tiny.text: One sigh: two inhales through the nose, then one long exhale through the mouth.

standard.text: 1–3 physiological sighs: inhale deep through the nose, add a short second inhale, then exhale slowly through the mouth.

stretch.text: 5 min of slow sighs, breathing in this pattern.

todo: kind = tool (engine-spec matrix 3-B), so the engine does not offer it as a Sprint patch.

title: Morning meditation
science_note: Focusing on your breath calms the body step by step.

tiny.text: In bed, close your eyes and take one slow breath through your nose.

standard.text: Right after waking, sit still for 5 min, eyes closed. Breathe slowly through your nose.

stretch.text: 5 min, and stay put even if you feel the urge to grab your phone.

title: Micro-rests
science_note: Short pauses help your brain lock in what you just learned.

tiny.text: Pause 10 s with your eyes closed. No phone.

standard.text: Between work blocks, pause 5–30 s. Close your eyes or look at nothing.

stretch.text: Take a 5–10 min break with no new input: no phone, no talking.

title: Afternoon sun
science_note: Late-day sun gives your body clock a second anchor and makes it less sensitive to light at night.

tiny.text: Step outside before sunset and look west.

standard.text: Late afternoon, before sunset: 10 min outside, facing the sun’s side of the sky. No sunglasses, not through a window.

stretch.text: Stay 15 min outside before sunset.

todo: Tiny '1 min' mirrors SL01's tiny version; it is not in the book.

title: Dim the lights
science_note: Even short bright light at night holds back melatonin and shifts your body clock.

tiny.text: Turn off the ceiling light. Use one low lamp.

standard.text: In your last hour before bed, keep lights dim and low: lamps, not ceiling lights.

stretch.text: Dim lights from sunset. Use red or amber bulbs at night, e.g. on the way to the bathroom.

title: Alcohol cutoff
science_note: Alcohol makes you drowsy but breaks up sleep and cuts deep, restoring sleep.

tiny.text: Pick a non-alcoholic drink tonight.

standard.text: No alcohol in the 8 hours before bed.

stretch.text: No alcohol today. Don’t use it to fall asleep.

title: Screens off
science_note: Screen light and busy content keep your brain alert and push sleep later.

tiny.text: Turn on Night Shift and lower screen brightness.

standard.text: No screens in the last hour before bed.

stretch.text: No screens for the last hour, and charge your phone outside the bedroom.

title: Mobility
science_note: Short mobility work keeps your wrists, back, knees, hips and shoulders moving well.

tiny.text: Deep sumo squat, palms together. Reach one arm up and follow it with your eyes, 3 times each side.

standard.text: 4 moves: deep sumo squat with twist, kneeling hip-flexor stretch, reverse tabletop, Founder pose.

stretch.text: Do the 4 moves on 2–4 days this week.

todo: The book says 2–4 times a week. The app ticks it like a daily patch until weekly targets exist.
Tiny time (1 min) is an estimate, not from the book.

title: Real food
science_note: Whole foods fill you up; ultra-processed mixes of starch, fat, sugar and salt drive overeating.

tiny.text: Swap one packaged snack for fruit or plain yogurt.

standard.text: Make this meal from whole, single-ingredient foods.

stretch.text: About 90% of today’s food unprocessed or minimally processed.

title: Fiber first
science_note: Fiber slows sugar spikes after meals and feeds your gut bacteria.

tiny.text: Add one handful of vegetables to this meal.

standard.text: Fill a third of your plate with fibrous vegetables.

stretch.text: Vegetables at every meal plus 2–3 whole fruits. Aim for 25–35 g fiber a day.

title: Fermented foods
science_note: Daily fermented foods raise gut-microbe variety and lower markers of inflammation.

tiny.text: Eat one spoon of plain yogurt, kimchi or sauerkraut.

standard.text: Have 2 servings of low-sugar fermented food today.

stretch.text: Have 2–4 servings today. Buy them from the fridge shelf, no added sugar.

title: Back to now
science_note: A wandering mind is an unhappy one. Pulling attention back to the present lifts mood.

tiny.text: Ask: “Is my mind on what I’m doing right now?”

standard.text: If not, ask one present-only question: what’s the room temperature? What do I smell?

stretch.text: Check in like this a few times through the day.

todo: Standard time (1 min) is an estimate, not from the book.

title: Two-column page
science_note: Splitting worries from what you can act on today stops the loop of rumination.

tiny.text: Write one worry, then one thing you can do about it today.

standard.text: Draw a line down a page. Left: your worries. Right: only what you can act on today.

stretch.text: Then work only on the right column.

todo: Time (5 min) is an estimate, not from the book.

title: Gratitude
science_note: A short daily gratitude practice is linked to lower blood pressure and better sleep.

tiny.text: Recall one moment someone thanked you.

standard.text: Swap one complaint for 1 min of gratitude. Best: recall a time someone truly thanked you.

stretch.text: Stay with it for 5 min.

title: Switch ritual
science_note: A short fixed ritual between roles clears the leftovers of the last task.

tiny.text: Before switching tasks, take 3 breaths with long exhales.

standard.text: Each time you switch roles (work to home, home to gym), do the same short ritual.

stretch.text: Do your ritual at every switch today, and skip the phone in between.

title: Alone time
science_note: Time alone without input lets your own thoughts and wants surface.

tiny.text: Sit alone, no phone, eyes closed, for one minute.

standard.text: 5 min fully alone: no phone, no people. Close your eyes and notice what comes up.

stretch.text: 10 min alone today, plus 1 hour for a hobby this week.
